segments: on the eve of the Feast of the Cross in Elul (September),
the Sultan burned the mangonels and departed,
and there was relief for the people of Melitene.
And in Nisan (April) of this year, John, emperor of the Greeks,
while hunting in Cilicia,
was gored by a wild boar and died.
And because his elder son was not near,
he commanded that his younger son Manuel should reign;
and he became king in Nisan of the year 1455
of the Greeks [1144 AD].
And when he entered Constantinople,
his brother received him and did homage to him,
and he was confirmed in the kingdom.
And also the king of the Franks of Jerusalem,
while hunting,
fell from his horse and died.
And his younger son Baldwin (the Third) was made king.
And because he was very young,
his mother administered the kingdom.
And in the year 1455
of the Greeks,
David, ruler of Hisn Ziyad (Kharpurt), also died,
and his younger son, Qara Arslan, succeeded him.
And because Arslan Doghmish, the elder son of David, was with Zengi, the lord of Mosul,
Zengi came to expel Qara Arslan
and to install Arslan Doghmish.
Now Qara Arslan went to Sultan Mas'ud of Iconium
and sought refuge with him.
He, in turn, gave him twenty thousand horsemen,
and he took them
and marched against Zengi.
Now when Zengi heard this,
he returned to his own territory.
And Mas'ud of Iconium again came and encamped against Melitene for three months,
and then abandoned it and departed,
because of the taking of Edessa from the Franks.
And in the year 1456
of the Greeks,
[1144 of our Lord],
when Joscelin, the lord of Edessa, had gone to Antioch,
the people of Harran informed Zengi, the lord of Mosul,
saying, "Edessa is empty of troops."
And Zengi gathered armies,
and on Tuesday, the twenty-eighth of the Latter Tishri (November), he came and encamped against Edessa.
And they pitched their camps at the Gate of the Hours,
near the Church of the Confessors.
And they set up against it seven mangonels,
and troops who shot arrows like torrents of rain.
And all the citizens of the city,
both great and small,
and the monks of the mountain,
were standing upon the wall and fighting.
And all the women were also upon the wall, handing up stones and water and food to the fighters.
